verdict.reasoning: The printed page (PDF p262, printed 240, 13.6.1) shows one Term/Subclause table of three rows: 77-level-entry / 13.11, constant-entry / 13.9, record-description-entry / 13.10. page-262.md lines 23-26 hold the first two as markdown table rows, then a blank line, then 'record-description-entry 13.10, Record description entry' as a loose paragraph. The row is cut off from the table. That is a real structural defect: anything that parses the table gets two of the three term-to-subclause mappings. The claim quotes both sources correctly. No wording is lost and the term and subclause still sit side by side in the prose, so the meaning a human reader takes away is unchanged. The defect is structural only, as the claim's severity already says.
